Automated PR Cleanup

Thank you for contributing to opencode.

Due to the high volume of PRs from users and AI agents, we periodically close older PRs using automated criteria so maintainers can focus review time on the most active and community-supported contributions.

This PR was closed because it matched the following cleanup criteria:

- The PR was created more than 1 month ago
- The PR had fewer than 2 positive reactions
- Positive reactions are counted as thumbs-up, heart, celebration, or rocket reactions on the PR

PRs created within the last month are not affected by this cleanup.

If you believe this PR was closed incorrectly, or if you are still actively working on it, please leave a comment explaining why it should be reopened. A maintainer can review and reopen it if appropriate.

Thanks again for taking the time to contribute.

This looks outdated on current OpenCode codepaths.

`AgentConfig.variant` now exists, agent-level `variant` is carried into the prompt/session model selection path, and variant options are resolved at request time. Agent `options` also appear to be merged into provider options.

That means the original blocker for static per-agent reasoning configuration in plugins like Weave appears to be resolved. Remaining gaps, if any, are narrower and more about variant discovery or dynamic SDK control than static config support.

I am seeing what looks like the same remaining workflow breakage on `1.15.6`.

Use case: the primary/main agent is intentionally restricted for some directories, but a delegated subagent should have its own broader permissions for those paths. After the permission inheritance changes, the effective scope feels mixed: the parent agent's local restrictions still affect the subagent, so a setup where "main cannot edit X, but subagent can edit X" is hard to express reliably.

No plugin is required for this behavior; plugins do not appear to affect this permission outcome.

This is not a request to bypass Plan Mode safety. It is the coordinator/executor case described in this thread: parent-local restrictions and child-agent permissions need to stay separable enough for delegated workflows.

Thanks, I checked #21728 and #21351. This looks related, but I don't think it is the same repro.

I'm using the experimental native background subagents path (`task(background=true)` / `task_status`), not a direct `POST /session/:id/prompt_async` notification and not a Plan/Build mode switch.

The main session had already switched to the new model and sent a normal message with it. Later, when the background subagent result was injected back into the main session, the main session model reset to the default.

I put together a minimal repro repo for this:

https://github.com/ualtinok/opencode-promptasync-runner-repro

It runs `opencode serve` against a fake OpenAI Responses API, installs one server plugin with a `repro_wait` tool, then starts an initial turn through the live listener. While that tool call is still running, the tool sends exactly one `input.client.session.promptAsync(...)` marker message.

On `opencode 1.15.7`, the script exits successfully with duplicate assistant children under the same marker user, for example:

```text
REPRODUCED: promptAsync marker user has 4 assistant children (2 stop).
```

The logs also show the plugin path being initialized a second time in the same PID immediately after the plugin-client prompt, which matches the split route/runtime hypothesis.

I think this is caused by the titlebar/tabs gating introduced in #28436 (`38b406fb3`, released in v1.15.6), rather than the controls being intentionally removed.

In `packages/app/src/components/titlebar.tsx` v1.15.6 has:

```tsx
<Match when={import.meta.env.VITE_OPENCODE_CHANNEL !== "prod"}>
```

But `VITE_OPENCODE_CHANNEL` is optional in `packages/app/src/env.d.ts`:

```ts
readonly VITE_OPENCODE_CHANNEL?: "dev" | "beta" | "prod"
```

For the standalone web / `opencode serve` build, this env can be `undefined`, so:

```ts
undefined !== "prod" // true
```

That means the new tabs/titlebar branch is enabled unintentionally for the web build, and the legacy titlebar portal mount points used by the search bar / terminal / file tree / diff/review controls are not present in the expected place.

I also checked v1.15.7 / current `dev`, and the same style of condition still appears as:

```ts
const USE_V2_TITLEBAR = import.meta.env.VITE_OPENCODE_CHANNEL !== "prod"
```

So this may still reproduce unless the build explicitly injects `VITE_OPENCODE_CHANNEL=prod`.

A safer fix would be to make the new titlebar opt-in instead of “not prod”, for example:

```ts
const USE_V2_TITLEBAR =
  import.meta.env.VITE_OPENCODE_CHANNEL === "dev" ||
  import.meta.env.VITE_OPENCODE_CHANNEL === "beta"
```

or additionally gate it to the intended desktop V2 path, while leaving standalone web on the legacy titlebar by default.

Same issue here — Windows 11, Windows Terminal, latest OpenCode.

The specific scenario: when the AI agent asks me a question via the interactive Q&A popup (the `question` tool), pressing Enter does nothing — the answer never submits. This happens consistently, not just during permission granting. Any dialog that requires Enter to confirm is affected.

**Current workaround**: Ctrl+C / Esc to dismiss the dialog (or force-close terminal if that doesn't work), then copy both the question and my intended answer, paste everything back into the TUI chat input, and resubmit as a regular message. Clunky, but keeps the session alive.

It seems like the root cause is that these overlay dialogs (permission, question, etc.) don't properly handle the Enter key event on Windows, possibly related to how OpenTUI processes keyboard input (similar to the `kpenter` vs `return` issue described in #17457).
